the decoy set has the following features: i) it is obtained from long molecular dynamics simulations of different initial conformations, some of them folding to a native conformation; ii) the structures obtained from the trajectories have a broad range of rmsd values; iii) it is possible to discriminate the native structure from the decoys with all the scoring functions tested.

the decoy set presented is suitable for testing energy scoring methods; the statistical energy function tested performs well in discriminating native-like conformations and the physical effective energies perform better in the case where the native structure is present in the set, but not when averaging over the MD trajectory is performed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the evaluation of the energy function in protein folding simulations and for the prediction of protein structure.
the development and application of methods to study the kinetics and thermodynamics of folding of a protein domain.
the development and evaluation of methods for estimating free energies of protein conformations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the statistical scoring functions perform better than the physical ones, and the combination of the statistical scoring functions performs better than any of the statistical scoring function used alone.
the energy functions are not able to distinguish between native and non-native conformations.

the statistical energy function (FRST) performs better than the two physical ones, GBSA and PBSA, when the native simulation snapshots are excluded, while the opposite is true if these snapshots are included.

the best results were obtained by the combination of statistical scoring functions (FRST), and that the best results for a single function were obtained by a combination of a contact and dihedral angle energy.
, for the present case, the best results are obtained with the FRST scoring function and the PBSA method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of different free energy methods and the comparison of the results is necessary to get reliable information on the quality of protein models.
, in general, statistical scoring functions are better suited for ranking decoys in a static set of structures, whereas physical energy functions perform better in the case of MD simulations.

the quality of the energy functions can be evaluated in a reliable manner only when the set is composed of snapshots from different simulations, and that the use of the average energy over the trajectory is not a good choice.
